la:verb:moveo.gloss: to move, stir, set in motion
senses: to move, stir, set in motion
to present or offer (an oblation or gift)
la:verb:moveo.html:
mŏvĕo, mōvi, mōtum, 2 (
sync., mōstis for movistis, ; mōrunt for moverunt,), v. a. and n.
Sanscr. mīv, set in motion; Gr. ἀμείβω, change; cf.: momentum, mutare
.
Act., to move, stir, set in motion; to shake, disturb, remove, etc. (syn.: cieo, agito, ago, molior).
Lit.: movit et ad certos nescia membra modos,: ut festis matrona moveri jussa diebus,to dance,: moveri Cyclopa, to represent a Cyclop by dancing (gesticulating), : et fila sonantia movit,struck,: citharam cum voce,: tympana,; to disturb: novis Helicona cantibus,: signum movere loco,to move from the place,: os,: gradum,i. e. to go forward, advance,: se, to move or bestir one's self: move ocius te,: praecepit eis, ne se ex eo loco moverent,not to stir from the spot,; : castra, to break up, remove: postero die castra ex eo loco movent,; ellipt. without castra: postquam ille Canusio moverat,: movisse a Samo Romanos audivit,.—Pass. reflex.: priusquam hostes moverentur,: hostem statu,to drive from his position, dislodge,: aliquem possessione,: heredes,to eject,: tribu centurionem,to turn out, expel,; so, aliquem de senatu,; the same also without senatu,: senatorio loco,to degrade,: ex agro,: move abs te moram,remove, cast off,: consulem de sententiā,to cause to recede, to dissuade,: litteram,to take away,.—Prov.: omnis terras, omnia maria movere,to turn the world upside down,.—
Transf.
To excite, occasion, cause, promote, produce; to begin, commence, undertake: exercitatione sudor movetur,is promoted, produced,: alvum,: dolorem,: lacrimas,to cause,: fletum populo,: risum,: alicui exspectationem,: indignationem,: misericordiam,: suspicionem,: ego istaec moveo, aut curo?begin, commence,: bellum,; : jam pugna se moverat,was going on,: cantūs,: tantum decus,begin,; cf. : nominis controversiam,to begin,; cf. ; : litem,: actionem,: mentionem rei,to make mention,: sacra,: movere ac moliri aliquid,to undertake any thing that excites disturbance,: ne quid moveretur,.—
To shake, to cause to waver, to alter: alicujus sententiam,to change, cause to waver,: sententiam regis,.—
To present, offer an oblation: ferctum Jovi moveto,.—
To disturb, concern, trouble, torment one: men moveat cimex Pantilius?: Armeniosne movet, Romana potentia cujus Sit ducis?; cf. . intoleranda vis aestūs omnium ferme corpora movit, : strepitu fora vestra,.—
Of plants, to put forth: si se gemmae nondum moveant,do not yet appear,: de palmite gemma movetur,

is produced, .—

To exert, exercise: inter principia condendi hujus operis, movisse numen ad indicandam tanti imperii molem traditur deos, (cf.: se movere, I. A. supra): artis opem,.—
= mutare, to change, transform: quorum Forma semel mota est,: nihil motum antiquo probabile est,.—
In mal. part., .—
Trop., to move, affect, excite, inspire: ut pulcritudo corporis movet oculos et delectat,charms,: quae me causae moverint,: fere fit, quibus quisque in locis miles inveteravit, uti multum earum regionum consuetudine moveatur,is much affected, influenced,: aliquem ad bellum,to stir up, excite,: movet feroci juveni animum conploratio sororis,stirs his anger,; cf. ; : numina Dianae,to irritate, provoke,: multa movens animo,to revolve, ponder, meditate,: moverat plebem oratio consulis,had stirred, made an impression on,: judicum animos,: acutule moveri,keenly affected,: neque illud me movet, quod, Caes. ap. , A. 2: affectus,: moveor etiam ipsius loci insolentiā,: nil moveor lacrimis, (4, 25, 5): absiste moveri,be not disturbed,: quos sectis Bellona lacertis Saeva movet,inspires, (al. monet): ut captatori moveat fastidia,excites nausea in,.—
Neutr., to move itself, move (very rare): terra dies duodequadraginta movit,an earthquake,; .—In pass.: reptile quod movetur,which moves itself, saep.—Hence,
mŏvens, entis, P. a., movable (class.): ex eā praedā, quae rerum moventium sit, movable things (as clothes, arms, furniture), : voluptas,that consists in motion,: furtum rerum moventium,.—Plur. subst.: quaedam quasi moventia,motives,.—Hence, adv.: mŏventer, movingly, affectingly (late Lat.), Schol. Bob. ad , n. 4.—
mōtus, a, um, P. a., moved, affected, disturbed (poet. and in post-class. prose): Ithaci digressu mota Calypso,: dictis,: precibus,.

la:verb:movens.html:
mŏvens, entis, Part. and P. a., v. moveo
fin. A.

la:verb:movendus.gloss: which is to be moved, set in motion
senses: which is to be moved, set in motion
which is to be disturbed, shaken.
which is to be aroused, excited, inspired.
Act., to move, stir, set in motion
